question: what does this checkpoint score on the rows, the label space and the split the teacher's 0.924 is quoted on, and in what ways is the protocol still not the same

cut.name: banking77-test
cut.rule: R7 — the reserved cut is read rarely and every read is logged with its date, its checkpoint and its reason

ours.ranking_beats_chance_decided_by: accuracy_options_only_ci95[0] > chance — the ranking with `unknown` taken out of the race, a diagnostic

baseline.what: the first accuracy this repo published at the full BANKING77 cardinality, and the one the phase-2 plan is written against
baseline.reading: indistinguishable from chance — the 95 % interval CONTAINS the chance rate. Not 'below chance': below would be a measured bias, and what is measured is the absence of signal
baseline.regime: trained at the sampler's K=3-8 with the backbone frozen (phase 1); scored here at K=77. R4: it is a phase-1 checkpoint measured under the phase-2 metric, which is exactly what makes it the baseline and not a target

references.setup: all 3 080 official test messages, 77 intents, category definitions + 24 labelled examples per prediction, no weight updates
references.caveat: BANKING77 is public; nobody can inspect Jev's training data, so this is not a held-out claim

references.setup: supervised fine-tune on the 10 003 training messages
references.caveat: trained ON this label space; our head never was

to_baseline.reading: the two intervals overlap, so this run has not been shown to differ from the first 77-way number this repo published

to_teacher.reading: a distance to a CITED number: the protocol differences in this artifact are part of it, and the arms of #T-option-text say how much of it the input information accounts for

chance.reading: R2 — the distance to chance is the first distance, because a number that does not clear it has no distance to anything else worth reading

rows.why: so 'same rows' is a set comparison and not an assertion — and so a future run that scores a different subset cannot publish its number under the same heading
rows.file_contents: one JSON object per row: id, gold, whether that gold was seen in training, our prediction, whether it was right, p(gold) and the gold's rank

basis.dataset_evidence: run.json: fence.clean_1m=True, fenced_datasets=['banking77', 'helpsteer2', 'pubmedqa']; the run's training sources are ['boolq', 'civil-comments', 'dbpedia14', 'detox-attack', 'email-triage', 'goemotions', 'huffpost', 'massive', 'prog-gold', 'snli', 'swag', 'synth-v1']

gold_exposure.why_two_routes: excluding the DATASET is not the same claim as the label strings being absent from the other sources; a run that fences banking77 and trains on a source that happens to use the same intent identifiers has seen those labels

unseen_gold.ranking_beats_chance_decided_by: accuracy_options_only_ci95[0] > chance — the ranking with `unknown` taken out of the race, a diagnostic

seen_gold.why_empty: no row of this cut has a gold on that side of the fence in this run

by_side.how: the same rows, the same K, the same forward pass — partitioned by whether the row's GOLD label was seen in training, not by cut and not by cardinality

information_regime.question: how much of the distance to the teacher is bought by WHAT THE MODEL IS SHOWN
information_regime.arms_quoted_from: each arm carries its own cut: A on banking77-test, B on banking77-test, C on banking77-dev, C-teacher-order on banking77-dev. The reserved cut is the rows this artifact scores; a development arm beside it is the same protocol measured on other rows of the same population, and is labelled as such

arithmetic.why: a difference between two arms is readable only when both were scored on the same rows; two arms on different cuts are two measurements and their difference carries the change of rows as well as the change of protocol

B - A on banking77-dev.reading: a point shift inside overlapping intervals is not a move: the information regime changed and the number did not

C - A on banking77-dev.reading: a point shift inside overlapping intervals is not a move: the information regime changed and the number did not

C-teacher-order - A on banking77-dev.reading: a point shift inside overlapping intervals is not a move: the information regime changed and the number did not

B - A on banking77-test.reading: a point shift inside overlapping intervals is not a move: the information regime changed and the number did not

budget_finding.reading: R8 — the teacher's regime does not fit in this window, so 'we reproduced the teacher's protocol' is false by budget before it is false by anything else

information_regime.reading: the information in the input explains none of the 0.9150 gap to the teacher — every arm stays inside the chance interval at K=77, n=1000, chance 0.012987 (A 0.0090 CI [0.004742, 0.017016], best B 0.0140 CI [0.008358, 0.023362], point shift +0.0050 = 0.5% of the gap and not distinguishable from zero), so #T-fullspace-objective keeps first priority with one competitor fewer

declared_fence.proves: the banking77 DATASET contributed zero rows to the mixture
declared_fence.does_not_prove: that no banking77 LABEL STRING occurs in the other sources — a different claim, and the one this scan measures

contamination.reading: no banking77 label occurs as an IDENTIFIER in the other 12 sources, and none is a gold answer anywhere in them. 7 occur only as the English phrase (['age_limit', 'country_support', 'exchange_rate', 'pending_transfer', 'receiving_money', 'verify_my_identity']…), which is a collision of language and not contamination: the model was never shown them as labels

not_auditable.what: the pretrained backbone's prior exposure to BANKING77
not_auditable.why: the backbone is a public checkpoint trained on a corpus this repo does not hold and cannot inspect. BANKING77 is a public benchmark, so exposure is plausible and unmeasurable
not_auditable.consequence: no claim in this repo — including 'unseen labels' — extends to the backbone's pretraining, and it is stated separately so the corpus fence's evidence is not read as covering it
not_auditable.same_for_the_teacher: and nobody can inspect the teacher's training data at all, which is why its 0.924 is not a held-out claim

same_rows_reading.value_means: NOT ESTABLISHED. It does not say the rows differ — nobody has compared them. `false` reads as 'this is a citation, not a same-rows measurement' (R3)
what_is_verified_on_our_side: the rows we scored are named one by one: 3080 ids of the form <dataset>:<dataset>-<row index within the split>:<question id>, digest 0cd9fb01c974ca74…
they are the sealed official test cut (`artifacts/splits/T-eval-cardinality-banking77-test`), whose seal is a content digest and not an intention
one line per row with its gold, our prediction and the gold's rank is written to the file this artifact names, so anybody can recompute our accuracy from the rows themselves
what_is_NOT_verified: the teacher has never been scored with our pipeline: 0.924 is read off a published report, and no forward pass of it has ever gone through `eval.calib.entries_from_samples`
there is no row-by-row evidence from the teacher's side — no per-row prediction list to align against our ids — so neither 'same rows' nor 'different rows' can be asserted

the information regime differs even where the rows do match: definitions and up to 24 retrieved examples against raw identifiers (R8), which makes two numbers on identical rows still not the same measurement
same_rows_reading.what_would_verify_it: either #T-teacher-probe scoring the teacher on these exact ids through our scorer (it needs a working API key), or a per-row prediction file published by the teacher that can be aligned to `rows.file`

protocol_differences.teacher: all 77 BANKING77 intents present on every row
protocol_differences.ours: all 77 intents present on every row, chance 0.012987
protocol_differences.evidence: every row is built with the whole sorted label space as its options (`eval.fullspace.full_samples`), and `cardinality` is published per row-set

protocol_differences.teacher: the 3 080 official test messages, per the published report
protocol_differences.ours: the 3080 official test messages, sealed by sha256 as `T-eval-cardinality-banking77-test`
protocol_differences.evidence: our side names every row it scored (`rows.ids_sha256`, and the per-row file); the teacher's side publishes a count and a split name, not a row list, so the two sets cannot be compared

protocol_differences.teacher: the teacher's own harness. It has never been scored through this repo's pipeline
protocol_differences.ours: `eval.calib.entries_from_samples` over a checkpoint in this repo, named by sha256
protocol_differences.evidence: `#T-teacher-probe` is the task that would score the teacher on our rows with our scorer; it needs a working API key and has not run

protocol_differences.teacher: none published: an aggregate accuracy, no per-row predictions
protocol_differences.ours: one line per row (id, gold, prediction, p(gold), rank of the gold) in the `rows.file` this artifact names
protocol_differences.evidence: with no per-row list on the other side there is nothing to align ours to, which is precisely why `same_rows` is UNVERIFIED rather than false

protocol_differences.teacher: a natural-language definition of each of the 77 categories
protocol_differences.measured: #T-option-text arm B replaces the identifiers with the teacher's own definitions: 37/3080 = 0.012013 CI [0.008728, 0.016514] against chance 0.012987 at K=77 on the banking77-test cut

protocol_differences.teacher: up to 24 BM25-retrieved labelled training examples per prediction
protocol_differences.ours: none — the row's own text and nothing else
protocol_differences.measured: #T-option-text arm C retrieves them the same way: 13/1000 = 0.013 CI [0.007613, 0.022114] against chance 0.012987 at K=77 on the banking77-dev cut

protocol_differences.dimension: how much of that context survives
protocol_differences.teacher: a context window large enough for the whole prompt
protocol_differences.measured: 11.886 of 23.982 retrieved examples survive the 256-token window, and in the teacher's own order the query itself survives in 0.001 of rows. The teacher's regime does not fit in this window, which is a result and not an excuse

protocol_differences.dimension: may the model decline to answer
protocol_differences.teacher: no: it names one of the 77 categories on every row
protocol_differences.ours: yes: the head scores [K + 1] and `unknown` can win, so our published accuracy is not a forced choice
protocol_differences.evidence: `abstain_rate` and `accuracy_options_only` (the same ranking with `unknown` taken out of the race) are published beside the headline, so the forced comparison is available without being the headline

protocol_differences.teacher: none claimed: no weight updates for the task
protocol_differences.ours: none on this label space — the head trained on 12 other sources at the sampler's K=3-8, with banking77 fenced
protocol_differences.evidence: `gold_exposure` in this artifact, computed from `run.json` and the contamination scan rather than asserted

protocol_differences.dimension: can the training data be inspected
protocol_differences.teacher: no. BANKING77 is public and nobody outside can look at what the teacher was trained on, so its number is not a held-out claim
protocol_differences.ours: yes for the 12 sources of the mixture: the fence is declared in `run.json` and the label strings are scanned for literally
protocol_differences.measured: 0 of 77 label strings occur as identifiers in the other sources and 0 as gold answers there — the fence excludes the DATASET, this scan is what excludes the STRINGS

protocol_differences.dimension: what the pretrained backbone had already seen
protocol_differences.ours: unknown and unauditable — a public web-scale pretrain is not something this repo can inspect either
protocol_differences.evidence: declared separately from the corpus fence on purpose: the fence is evidence, this is an absence of evidence, and merging them would let the second borrow the credibility of the first

cost.note: the head attends BETWEEN options, so this grows about K² per row: a cost measured at K=8 does not price K=77

honesty: the teacher's 0.924 is a CITATION. It was not produced by this pipeline and there is no per-row evidence to align against ours, so this artifact publishes a distance to a quoted number, not a head-to-head result
every difference of protocol we know of is enumerated above with `matched: true | false | unverifiable`; the third value is not a polite way of saying false
R2 — no accuracy in this file appears without its cardinality, its chance rate and its 95 % interval
R4 — a verdict measured in one training regime does not transfer to another; the baseline is a phase-1 checkpoint read under the phase-2 metric and is kept as a line, not a target
reason: #T-jev-parity: verify the parity artifact is emitted by the run's own gate without manual intervention (done-when 6); same checkpoint and same rows as the 0.0123 baseline, re-scored on CPU because MPS is held by the bigk-fullspace job
parity_line: [banking77-test RESERVED] 38/3080 = 0.012338 CI [0.009002, 0.016888] at K=77 against chance 0.012987 — does not clear its chance rate; 0.911662 from the teacher's cited 0.924 and +0.000000 from the first published 77-way number 0.012338. The two protocols differ on 7 declared dimensions (scored-by, row-evidence, option-text, labelled-examples, context-budget, abstention, training-data-audit) and 2 cannot be checked from either side (split, backbone-exposure), so same_rows stays UNVERIFIED: the teacher has never been scored through this pipeline and publishes no per-row evidence to align against ours

emitted_by.how: composed from the rows that run had already scored — no extra forward pass and no extra read of the reserved cut
